subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit soft-steer lifecycle that interrupts or pauses active generation/tool work, injects user input, and resumes with partial context, or should supported steering remain boundary-based?
rationale: Current OpenClaw and Codex contracts support boundary steering and separate interrupt behavior; the requested combined lifecycle changes runtime semantics, channel UX, and fallback behavior.

options.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
options.body: Add a separate mode or command with explicit pause/abort, partial-output, context replay, backend rejection, and fallback semantics.

options.title: Keep Boundary Steering
options.body: Document current steer semantics as the supported behavior and use narrower issues only for messages reaching the existing active-run queue policy.

options.title: Broaden Default Steer
options.body: Make default steer use the stronger interrupt/resume lifecycle after upgrade and runtime compatibility proof.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
recommendation.body: Add a separate mode or command with explicit pause/abort, partial-output, context replay, backend rejection, and fallback semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available routing owner from prior maintainer replacement work and shared active-run steering history.
